```{r}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  out.width = "100%",
  asciicast_at = "all",
  asciicast_cursor = TRUE
)
asciicast::init_knitr_engine(
  echo = TRUE,
  echo_input = TRUE
)
options(cli.progress_show_after = 0)
options(cli.progress_clear = FALSE)
options(cli.progress_format_iterator = NULL)
options(cli.progress_format_iterator_nototal = NULL)
options(cli.progress_format_tasks = NULL)
options(cli.progress_format_tasks_nototal = NULL)
options(cli.progress_format_download = NULL)
options(cli.progress_format_download_nototal = NULL)
```

You can use `capture_plot` to capture the plot (In theory, any format works, including `ggplot2`) in R session.

```{asciicast}
#' label: "example_capture"
library(rviuer)
p <- draw_pixels("rviuer") 
p
```

```{asciicast}
p |>
  capture_plot(width = 40, height = 10) |>
  render_plot()
```

You can also use file path directly.

```{asciicast}
#' label: "example_file_path"
#' asciicast_speed: 2
url  <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tidyverse/dplyr/main/man/figures/logo.png"
tmp <- tempdir()
dest <- file.path(tmp, "logo.png")

download.file(url, destfile = dest, mode = "wb")
render_plot(dest)
```
